text:
maya: Heads-up — observed a weird cluster of preemptions in eu-west3 between 02:10-02:25 UTC, dashboards spiked but noisy. opening a single thread to collect notes.
jonah: saw that too, noticed network errors aligning with eviction events. could be provider-side scheduling + transient network flap.
sasha: can you paste the panel? i saw the preemptions rate jump to ~12% for a 5m window. that sounds high. :alarm_clock:
maya: pasted: Grafana panel link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ops/spot-availability?view=eu-west3 (only available on VPN)
maya: quick snippet of the query we use:
```
max_over_time(preemptions_total{region="eu-west3"}[5m]) / max_over_time(spot_capacity{pool="a100"}[5m])
```
arun: that query is noisy when capacity churns. i think we should smooth and combine with eviction_score + net_err_rate before firing alerts.
liam: agree. propose: ensemble metric = weighted_sum( eviction_confidence, preempt_rate_norm, net_err_rate_norm ) then alert if ensemble > 0.7 for 10m. reduces false positives from single-signal blips.
jonah: +1. also add a minimum absolute capacity threshold so tiny pools don't trigger. e.g. only if pool_total_gpus >= 8.
sasha: can we backfill a week to validate? want precision/recall numbers. i can run an ad-hoc job to compute TP/FP vs incidents.
maya: pls run backfill 2026-02-28 -> 2026-03-05. label incidents from PD and incidents/ie logs. maybe we tune weights.
arun: wrote a quick prom query idea for ensemble:
```
spot_sensor_fusion_v1{region="eu-west3"}
  = 0.5*label_replace(avg_over_time(eviction_confidence[10m]), "", "", "", "")
  + 0.3*(increase(preemptions_total[10m]) / 1 + increase(preemptions_total[10m]))
  + 0.2*avg_over_time(net_err_rate[10m])
```
jonah: that prom pseudo looks rough but fine as a start. we should export a confidence label and keep it as a metric so dashboards can color by confidence.
liam: ops note: rolling median(20m) reduces alert churn a lot vs simple avg. also add "suppression windows" after a provider maintenance notice.
infra-bot: scheduled job created: backfill-spot-fusion-20260304 by sasha -> status: queued. (run id: fj-4881)
sasha: running now on batch cluster. i'll post results in this thread when done.
maya: SLO check — during the spike p50 latency didn't change much, p95 up ~0.4% overall for the region. not catastrophic but worth tracking as a regression.
jonah: we should make the alert include expected SLO impact: alert if ensemble > 0.7 AND slo_error_rate_delta > 0.25%. that helps prioritize.
arun: agree. also add routing: if confidence >= 0.9 -> oncall page, else -> infra channel. we keep oncall noise low.
liam: cost angle: if we start hedging (fallback to on-demand) automatically during high-confidence events we should estimate cost delta and annotate the incident. e.g. fallback would spend ~+18% on those minutes.
sasha: backfill finished. preliminary: ensemble@0.7 gives 78% precision, 64% recall on labeled incidents in the week. i've uploaded CSV to /mnt/analysis/spot-fusion-backfill-20260304.csv and added a small notebook.
maya: awesome. next steps: 1) refine weights 2) create grafana panel for confidence 3) update alerting rule with capacity floor and slo delta 4) add runbook for hedging cost estimates and opt-out flags.
jonah: i'll draft the alert PR and a small playbook for responders (how to check provider status, common mitigations).
liam: i'll add a dashboard tile that simulates cost if we hedged for X minutes given current traffic.
arun: timeline: can we aim for rollout to staging in 3 days, prod in 10?
maya: fine with that timeline. thanks all. tagging @pagerduty-bot — if we flip routing logic we'll need PD rule update.
pagerduty-bot: noted. submit PD rule change ticket referencing incident-runbook-spot-fusion-20260304.
jonah: PR incoming later today. will link here. :thumbsup:
maya: closing the loop — will follow up after the alert PR and the dashboard patch. thanks team.
